assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic and satiety actions) led to long-acting agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits. Originality, clarity of the mechanism and breadth of clinical impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and therapeutic rationale of GLP-1 and GLP-2 over decades; Knudsen led the design of acylated, long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's early peptide characterization and credit relative to others (e.g. Habener, who is not on the list) is disputed, so a three-person configuration necessarily leaves out some contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed by many independent trials and by wide clinical use; the discovery is mature and its recognition is timely, with evidence still accumulating for long-term outcomes.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener and others for the original peptide identification is contested and from memory I cannot verify the details.
Whether the prize should reward the physiology, the drug development, or both.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience cell-type-specific, millisecond-precision control of neural activity, enabling causal circuit dissection across species, including motor and brainstem circuits. It is a methodological invention with very broad, lasting use across biology.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth's group and Boyden demonstrated neuronal use and generalization; Miesenböck made an earlier genetically targeted photostimulation. The credited list has six names, so a three-person limit leaves out deserving contributors, with Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck the main omissions.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in thousands of studies; the technique is mature, and early clinical applications (retinal restoration) are emerging.
uncertainties: Unavoidable exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck under the three-laureate rule.
Whether a methods prize is preferred over a disease-mechanism discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells, including CAR-T therapy, produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now myeloma; this is a new treatment modality with clear conceptual origin and strong clinical proof.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed and clinically validated costimulation-enhanced CARs; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells for cancer. Eshhar and others (not on the list) made earlier CAR contributions, so credit is not entirely clean.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up; recognition is timely. Solid-tumor efficacy and toxicity remain open.
uncertainties: Early CAR concept credit (Eshhar and others) is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VLP-based HPV vaccines are a rare case of a vaccine that prevents cancer, with population-level falls in infection and cervical precancer. The impact is substantial and the discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP platform; Frazer's group (with Zhou) independently developed VLP vaccine technology, and Zhou's death complicates credit. Mechanism and attribution are reasonably clean for three, but earlier zur Hausen recognition covers the virus-cancer link.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of surveillance data show strong effectiveness against cervical neoplasia; recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for Jian Zhou in the Frazer work is not captured in the credited names.
Possible view that the cancer link was already recognized by the 2008 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a fatal childhood neuromuscular disease into a treatable one and established splicing-modifying oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class. Mechanistic basis and clinical benefit are both well demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target and Bennett developed the antisense chemistry and drug; the pairing is a coherent two-person prize. Contributions of Singh, Hua and others on the target are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term data; recognition is timely though still moderately recent.
uncertainties: Other contributors to target identification may need recognition.
Breadth beyond SMA is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and links to disease, aging and cancer. It is a conceptually original, foundational discovery in cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily dissected the pathway, from IRE1/HAC1 to ATF6 in mammals; a two-person prize is natural, though Ron and others also contributed to later arms (PERK/CHOP).
assessment.maturity: Core mechanism is long established and replicated; disease relevance is still being translated therapeutically.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is less direct than for clinical candidates.
Contributions of Ron and Shen on the PERK arm are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition by imatinib created the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting CML from a lethal to a chronic disease; later work on resistance mutations guided successor drugs.
assessment.attribution: Druker led clinical translation, Lydon led the chemistry and kinase inhibitor program, and Sawyers uncovered resistance mechanisms and dasatinib. Rowley, Witte and others made the underlying discovery, and Nowell and Hungerford, Rowley and Baltimore are often cited, so the pool is large; Lasker 2009 already honored Druker, Lydon and Sawyers.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of outcome data; fully mature and perhaps late.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with earlier-recognized foundational work on the Philadelphia chromosome and ABL.
Whether a drug-development story fits the committee's preference at this point.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency subthalamic and thalamic stimulation provides durable symptom control in Parkinson's disease and tremor and opened neuromodulation as a therapeutic field in neurology and psychiatry; I am more cautious about mechanism, which is still debated.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the single credited name and is widely associated with the high-frequency stimulation concept; Benazzouz, Limousin, Hallett and DeLong contributed through the subthalamic target and the basal ganglia model, so a sole prize is questionable from an allocation standpoint.
assessment.maturity: Established clinical practice for more than three decades with extensive replication; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Sole-laureate attribution may be unfair given the credited names supplied.
The mechanism of action of high-frequency stimulation remains debated.
